messages:
mike: Bringing up lilac17b-int4 on canary. initial smoke looked fine but hit OOMs under realistic prompts.
anya: ugh. earliest OOMs at batch=4, max_new_tokens=1024? what hw?
mike: g5x2 nodes. 80GB. pattern: coldstart OK, but after a few long sessions memory usage climbs and then OOMs. logs show many small KV allocs.
cheng: do we see fragmentation or a leak? can you paste the allocation trace from runtime?
mike: pasted below. looks like repeated allocations around these calls:

```
2026-03-18T21:10:02Z runtime: kv_cache.alloc segment=128k count=72
2026-03-18T21:10:02Z runtime: prefetch.start depth=6 seq_len=1024
2026-03-18T21:10:03Z runtime: kv_cache.alloc segment=16k count=420
2026-03-18T21:10:05Z runtime: oom: alloc_failed size=1.2MB context=evict
```

mike: note the 420 tiny segments right after prefetch. smells like degenerate prefetch.
anya: did quant step change layout/padding? int4 can amplify small-allocation patterns.
cheng: we tried int8 -> int4 in one pass? any sharding changes?
mike: this model used the new per-layer grouping quantizer (experimental) + windowed prefetch. suspect interaction.
yuki: quick experiment idea: disable prefetch depth >2 and run steady-state PIC (prefetch-incremental-cushion) to see if tiny segments vanish.
anya: also try lowering default max_new_tokens for canary route to 256. many customers don't need 1k by default and it's the largest driver of long KV lifetimes.
cheng: agree. lowering max_new_tokens will reduce prefix+gen memory. but we should bisect: is it quantizer or prefetch? do 2 canaries: (A) original quant + prefetch depth=2, (B) fallback to int8 quant + original prefetch.
mike: running both now. kickoff commands:

```
# run canary A
curl -s -X POST https://internal.redwood/canary/run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"lilac17b-int4","policy":{"prefetch_depth":2,"slot_reserve":0.06}}'

# run canary B (int8 fallback)
curl -s -X POST https://internal.redwood/canary/run \
  -d '{"model":"lilac17b-int8","policy":{"prefetch_depth":6}}'
```

sre-bot: canary A started on node pool g5x2-canary-3 (run id a3f2). canary B started on node pool g5x2-canary-4 (run id b1c7).
mike: first 30 minutes: A stable, no tiny-seg spike. B shows same tiny allocations and then OOM for one session.
anya: that points to quantizer change as culprit? weird—int8 shows problem but int4 is fine in A because prefetch was reduced.
cheng: so it's an interplay: prefetch depth amplifies a quantizer-induced allocation pattern. root cause = quant layout causes many small cache entries when prefetch creates many small KV entries.
yuki: mitigation path:
- short term: reduce default max_new_tokens for lilac17b canary and prod to 256
- disable aggressive prefetch (depth>2) for int8/int4 variants until we patch quantizer
- bump slot_reserve to 6% for canary nodes for extra headroom
- add a regression test to eval harness that runs mixed-length templated prompts to catch fragmentation

mike: implemented short-term defaults on dev routing: max_new_tokens=256, prefetch_depth=2 for canary lanes. monitoring: memory churn down 70% and no OOMs 2h in.
anya: nice. can we try a targeted quantizer fix? maybe coalesce small KV segments at allocation time or force minimal granularity of 64k.
cheng: there's a lightweight patch: coalesce_alloc(true) in kv_cache when segment<32k and adjacent free found. low-risk.
yuki: please gate behind perf test; coalesce might slightly increase tail latency. add a perf A/B with 1000 short requests and 100 long ones.
mike: created PR #4872 with coalesce_alloc and tests. bench looks OK: median latency +0.8ms, p99 unchanged. mem defrag stat improved.
sre-bot: PR #4872 deployed to canary pool g5x2-canary-3. auto-smoke passed.
anya: once canary passes 24h, we should roll to dedicated staging and then prod. release checklist item: update docs about default max_new_tokens for lilac17b and note the guardrails.
cheng: also add a model card note: quantizer complexity interacts with prefetch heuristics; recommend conservative prefetch for newly onboarded quant variants.
yuki: action items:
- mike: monitor canary for 48h and post a slack summary
- cheng: add regression to eval harness
- anya: update routing defaults and docs
- mike: if canary stable, roll coalesce to prod with slot_reserve bump

mike: noted. early numbers: canary memory churn metric down from 12GB/min to 3.4GB/min, error rate 0 -> 0.02% at 3h. will report back.
anya: great. thanks team :thumbsup:
mike: thanks all. tagging @oncall for visibility in case residual issues pop up.
